candidates.attacker_control: The attacker supplies the search text that the embedding application passes to the public LIKE APIs: `where(entity.getField()).like(userInput)`, `.notLike(...)`, `.any(...)`, `.startsWith(...)`, `.endsWith(...)` (ConditionBuilder.java:237-278, exposed via OnGoingStringCondition/OnGoingLikeCondition). Any value containing a single quote terminates the generated string literal and allows appending HQL syntax; wildcard wrapping only surrounds the injected text with `%` characters.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched the whole source for escaping/sanitization (no `escape`, `StringEscapeUtils`, quote replacement, or PreparedStatement-style handling); confirmed LikeCondition.getParameters() is empty and DefaultQueryBuilder only binds ValueParameter instances, so the value cannot be bound elsewhere; confirmed ValueParameter and all other conditions (EqualCondition, SingleParameterCondition, BetweenCondition, InCondition, MemberOfCondition) use named parameters; examined Type.wrap and found it only prepends/appends `%`; considered that the API Javadoc does not promise sanitization, but since all sibling value APIs parameterize their inputs, callers reasonably expect the same of like(); considered HQL-vs-SQL parsing differences (impact depends on provider) and noted that no runtime exploit was executed.
candidates.impact: HQL/JPQL injection: an attacker can break out of the string literal and alter the query's predicate logic, e.g. widen or eliminate application filters or append additional HQL conditions/subqueries, which can expose records the application intended to exclude and can enable boolean/error-based inference over data reachable through HQL subqueries. It also defeats the library's parameterization guarantee. No native SQL execution, command execution, or direct credential access is claimed; the precise blast radius depends on the entity model and JPA provider.
candidates.prerequisites: Typical use of the library as a query builder where a LIKE condition value originates from an untrusted source (e.g., a search form or request parameter), followed by execution through Query.list()/get() or getQuery() passed to EntityManager.createQuery(); the JPA provider (e.g., Hibernate) parses the resulting HQL.
candidates.root_cause: LikeCondition stores the caller-supplied `toMatch` string and interpolates it verbatim into the query fragment: `selector.createQueryFragment(incrementor) + " " + getLike() + " '" + type.wrap(toMatch) + "' "` (LikeCondition.java:86-89). `type.wrap(...)` only adds `%` wildcards (lines 32-59), never escapes or quotes the value, and `getParameters()` returns `Collections.emptyList()` (lines 103-106), so no ValueParameter (`:name`) is generated. By contrast, every other value comparison routes through `selector.generateParameter(value)` -> ValueParameter.generate() (`:`+name, ValueParameter.java:51-57) and is bound in DefaultQueryBuilder.createJPAQuery via `query.setParameter(...)` (lines 430-434). No escaping helper (e.g., quote doubling) exists anywhere in the source. As a result the LIKE value is reachable as raw query syntax.
candidates.title: HQL injection via LIKE condition values concatenated into query text instead of being bound as parameters
candidates.trace: Torpedo.where(entity.getName()) returns a ConditionBuilder as OnGoingStringCondition -> ConditionBuilder.like(String)/notLike(String)/any()/startsWith()/endsWith() -> private createLike() constructs LikeCondition/NotLikeCondition with the raw value (ConditionBuilder.java:254-278) -> DefaultQueryBuilder.appendWhereClause -> LikeCondition.createQueryFragment returns selector text + " like '" + wrappedValue + "' " -> DefaultQueryBuilder.freezeQuery assembles the full query string -> createJPAQuery calls entityManager.createQuery(getQuery(...)); DefaultQueryBuilder.getParameters/getValueParameters only collects ValueParameter/SubqueryValueParameters instances (Condition.java:50-60), and LikeCondition contributes none, so the value is never bound via setParameter.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Exploitability depends on the embedding application routing untrusted input into a LIKE-family call and on the JPA provider accepting the injected HQL; a concrete payload's ability to read data from other entity types via HQL subqueries was not verified. No test sources are present in the snapshot to confirm intended behavior.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-89/CWE-943 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in HQL Query (HQL/JPQL injection)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the full assigned snapshot: 122 source files (all under src/main/java; no test directory), pom.xml, README, .travis.yml. Read in full or in relevant part every query-construction path: all condition classes (LikeCondition, NotLikeCondition, SingleParameterCondition and subclasses, BetweenCondition, InCondition, InSubQueryCondition, MemberOfCondition, PolymorphicCondition, LogicalCondition/LogicalElement/GroupingCondition, EmptyLogicalCondition), ConditionBuilder, Condition/AbstractCondition/ConditionHelper, DefaultQueryBuilder (assembly + execution), ValueParameter/SelectorParameter/SubqueryValueParameters, all handler classes (Parameter/Where/Grouping/Join/Custom/Constant/Function/OrderBy/Math), selector and join classes, and the proxy/reflection utilities (TorpedoMagic, TorpedoMethodHandler, ProxyFactoryFactory, MultiClassLoaderProvider, SerializableMethod). Targeted literal searches for Class.forName, reflection invocation, escaping, String.format/MessageFormat, ObjectInputStream, ProcessBuilder, and createQueryFragment were used to enumerate raw string sinks.
limitations: No code was executed, no build/tests/scanners were run, and no runtime confirmation of exploitation was obtained; findings are source-level leads only.
The snapshot contains no test sources, so intended/expected behavior (e.g., whether LIKE values were ever meant to be escaped) could not be cross-checked against tests.
The reviewer cannot inspect git history, patches, upstream advisories, or sibling conditions; whether a fix exists in another revision is unknown.
Some trivial interfaces/enums were not read line-by-line, but they contain no query-fragment construction; search covered all files for the relevant sinks.
Impact of the HQL injection (e.g., whether subqueries can cross entity boundaries) depends on the JPA provider and entity model and was reasoned about, not demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: CustomFunctionHandler builds `name + "(%1$s)"` and String.format()s it into the query (handlers/CustomFunctionHandler.java:42-53) via Torpedo.function(name, type, value).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an application to pass attacker-controlled data as the function name; normal usage supplies a hard-coded function name. Plausible misuse, but far weaker attacker-control evidence than the LIKE path.

rejected_leads.lead: ConstantFunctionHandler / ComparableConstantFunctionHandler inline `constant.toString()` directly into the query (handlers/ConstantFunctionHandler.java:46-48, ComparableConstantFunctionHandler.java:46-48).
rejected_leads.reason: Design intends literal constant expressions supplied by the developer; injection requires misuse, and no escaping contract exists for constants.
The class name derives from a developer-constructed object, not from request-controlled text; no attacker-controlled input path identified.

rejected_leads.lead: TorpedoMagic stores the current proxy in a ThreadLocal without remove() (internal/TorpedoMagic.java:30-57), and MultiClassLoaderProvider keeps an unbounded static classloader cache (utils/MultiClassLoaderProvider.java:32-91).
rejected_leads.reason: State/resource-management smells without a demonstrated confidentiality or integrity impact; not a source-evidenced vulnerability on their own.
The cloned object is constructed internally from the query DSL; no untrusted serialized stream is accepted, so no deserialization vulnerability is demonstrated.

summary: TorpedoQuery is an HQL/JPA query builder. Most comparison values (eq/neq/lt/lte/gt/gte/in/notIn) are safely bound as named parameters, but the LIKE-family APIs interpolate the raw caller-supplied string directly into the generated query text with only surrounding single quotes and no escaping. `LikeCondition.createQueryFragment()` (src/main/java/org/torpedoquery/jpa/internal/conditions/LikeCondition.java:86-89) builds `... like '<toMatch>'`, `getParameters()` returns an empty list, and the tainted string is ultimately handed to `EntityManager.createQuery()` in `DefaultQueryBuilder.createJPAQuery()` (lines 415-434) without `setParameter` binding. Because a single quote is not escaped or doubled anywhere in the repository, an attacker-controlled value containing `'` can terminate the literal and inject HQL. This is the strongest distinct issue found; other raw-concatenation sites require developer-controlled inputs and are noted as rejected leads.
